title: Castle v4: the Great Keep
status: proposal for review (design only, nothing built)

conventions.cells: island cells, 1 cell = 1 m; x east, z south (north is -Z), as src/data/zoneMaps.ts and CASTLE_PLAN
conventions.rects: [x0, z0, x1, z1] in cell edges
conventions.heights: metres above the crown (the bailey ground, world y 11) unless a key ends in _world

curtain.note: One rectangle, symmetric about the main axis; wall walk at +7 between crenellated parapets. Every tower projects outward into the moat, so the inside faces stay straight and buildings and gardens can stand against them.

runs.note: dies into the keep's north-west turret

curtain.wall_walk_access: through the gatehouse's drums (a door at the foot of each, inside the gate); every tower opens onto the walk

tower_spacing: about 21 to 23 m on every face: corner, three wall towers, corner on the west and east; corner, wall tower, gatehouse, wall tower, corner on the south; the keep breaks the north

gatehouse.note: today's gatehouse unchanged, moved onto the new axis: two D-towers 6 either side, a passage 4 wide under the ceremonial arch, the block a storey over the curtain, flags on the drums and the lord's banner over the arch. Its drums stay flat so the keep's spires rise over the gate front seen from below the rock

keep.note: A massive square keep on the axis, standing on the terrace with its back three metres beyond the north curtain at the brink of the tear face; its front turrets are the hinges between its face and the wings' fronts, which die into their drums. Four round corner turrets rise a stage above its parapet to blue spires; a projecting frontispiece on the axis carries the great door and the showpiece window between two slender pinnacles.

storeys.what: ground: the throne hall, two storeys high
upper: galleries round the throne hall
second: the lord's great chamber (closed for now)
third: the map room and the treasury (closed for now)

keep.parapet: machicolated and crenellated, cut from the same cream stone as the walls (no stuck-on trim in another colour), a plain gilt band under it

frontispiece.crest: the lord's shield, carved and gilt, between the showpiece window and the parapet

great_door.note: the ceremonial arch scaled up: a deep ring of voussoirs and a hood mould cut from the same stone, oak leaves with gilt hinges; the lord's crest in the tympanum instead of the gold diamond

windows_south.what: blank but for one small lancet high in each bay
the showpiece: one great window with stone tracery over the door, lighting the throne hall
two tall lancets in each bay under hood moulds
a pair of lights under one hood in each bay
small square-headed lights under the parapet
slit lights stepping up round each drum with the spiral stair inside

keep.window_rule: sizes fall storey by storey (tall, paired, small) on two axes per side bay; one showpiece only; glass clear and lightly tinted so the room shows through

ground.note: the throne on a three-step dais against the north wall on the axis, the lord's banners behind and braziers either side; a crimson runner from the great door; four great piers carry the galleries
straight flight along the south wall, climbing west from beside the door
the lord's door onto the great hall's dais
onto the chapel's west end (the lord's pew)

upper.note: behind the showpiece window; the two stairs arrive at its ends
over the throne, looking down the hall

terrace.note: The upper court: a raised terrace along the whole north range, a dressed retaining wall with an open balustrade on its edge; the keep's podium projects on the axis to carry the grand stair.

stairs.note: on the axis, 12 wide, between cheek walls ending in pedestals that carry the two champions
from the terrace down into the kitchen garden on its axis
its mirror, down into the privy garden

buildings.note: today's kitchen at the hall's service end, open to its roof: two hearths, the buttery and pantry along its south end; two tall chimneys

today's residence range turned round: the screens and the stair to the minstrel gallery at the west end, the hall open to its roof with its central hearth and long tables, the high table on the dais at the keep end; galleries on its north and east sides
buildings.windows: three tall paired windows between buttresses; the hall door under a porch at the screens end

buildings.note: the chapel, open to its roof, the altar at its east end and the lord's pew at the keep end; a slender bellcote
buildings.windows: tall lancets between buttresses and one rose window over its south door

buildings.note: the lord's lodging: a day room below, the solar above; chimneys
buildings.windows: an oriel window on the upper floor over the terrace and the privy garden

buildings.note: six stalls off a central aisle and a tack room, the hay loft over them; the arched door in its east gable closes the cross walk on the axis; stall half-doors onto the stable yard, a back door into the paddock
buildings.windows: half-doors with horses looking out, a loft door with a hoist beam over the gable door

buildings.note: the stables' mirror: the guardroom and the armory off a central passage, the dormitory in the loft; the arched door in its west gable closes the cross walk; a back door into the training yard
buildings.windows: small square windows with shutters, a loft door over the gable door

zones.note: four boxed quarters of vegetables round a well on its own axis; the stair comes down into it from the terrace; gates onto the north walk and into the stable yard; fruit trees trained flat on its walls

the lord's flower garden: lawn, four flower beds round a small basin, the rose arbour against the east wall and two shade trees; the stair comes down into it from the terrace; gates onto the north walk and into the muster yard
setts between the kitchen garden and the stables: the stall doors, the trough against the stable wall, a mounting block; open to the side walk
the stable yard's mirror before the barracks: weapon racks against the wall and the well
grass behind a post-and-rail fence, its gate on the side walk, the stables' back door opening into it: 20 by 25, three times today's
the paddock's mirror: the lists (pells either side of a lane) and the archery butts behind a shooting line, fenced, its gate on the side walk
the cour d'honneur at the grand stair's foot, lawns with clipped yews either side, a pair of lamps
the arrival court inside the gate between lawns and clipped yews, two lamps
the dragon fountain at the crossing of the axes
four box-edged lawn panels round the plaza, each cut back in an arc to the basin; flower borders, clipped cones and a blossom tree in each outer corner; no statues
everything else inside the curtain is clipped lawn: either side of the cour (with yews) and of the forecourt (with yews)

walks.note: from the stair foot through the plaza to the gate
from the stables' door through the plaza to the barracks' door

features.note: today's bronze dragon (pick A) on its pedestal, moved with the axis
on the grand stair's west cheek pedestal, with a new helmet
today's rose pergola, against the east wall

water.note: Two springs spill from the moat's head walls beside the north corner towers. The moat rings the west, south and east walls at one level two metres below the turf (the north stands on the brink of the tear face). It leaves over a weir under the gate terrace on the axis and falls down the south face into a pool, from which the stream runs on to the pond; on the west it also overflows off the buttress into the Veil (today's west fall).

moat.banks: a dressed stone revetment with a coping of the same stone on the outer side; the curtain and towers rise straight out of the water on battered plinths

springs.note: out of a mossy cleft in the west arm's head wall, spilling down two metres into the moat
its mirror at the east arm's head

outlet.note: a weir and an arched culvert under the gate terrace; the water pours from an arch in the bastion's face

falls.note: on the axis below the gate terrace, into the pool
the moat's overflow, by a slot through the lip of the west buttress, into the Veil (today's west fall)

water.stream_note: from the pool along the foot of the rock to rejoin today's course at (98, 138); the pond is unchanged

approach.note: The climb arrives at the landing outside the moat's south-east corner; the ledge road runs west along the south front between two walls, the moat on its castle side, to the gate terrace on the axis; the bridge crosses the moat to the gate. A matching walled walk runs west from the terrace to a lookout at the south-west corner, so the south front is symmetric.

gate_terrace.note: a bastion out over the cliff: two lamps, two banner poles at the bridge's foot, the moat's outlet under it

bridge.note: two low stone arches over the water and a lowered drawbridge span at the gate end, parapets both sides

ledge_road.walls: an inner parapet on the moat side and an outer parapet on the cliff side, one coping line; lamps inside the outer wall

ledge_walk.note: the road's mirror west of the terrace

landing.note: walled all round except where the road leaves it and the climb comes in

lookout.note: the landing's mirror: a walled terrace over the farm and the Veil, a bench and two lamps

climb.note: today's climb with one bend, so it keeps its grade up to the moved landing

crown.note: The crown grows to carry the moat: north to the tear edge (the keep's back on the brink), about six metres at the north-west corner (new land on the tear), the north-east shoulder raised to the crown, about four metres on the east and five to nine on the south (the moat, the ledge and its bastions).

stay: the gatehouse, as built (moved 10 m east onto the new axis)
the dragon fountain (moved with the axis)
the parterre (narrower, four panels, no statues)
curtain kit, drum towers, the banners on every run
the kitchen and today's residence range (re-planned as the great hall and kitchen)
the rose arbour (into the privy garden)
the ledge road, the climb and the landing (moved)
shrink_or_change: the stables grow into a range of six stalls with a hay loft
the barracks shrink to a one-storey range with a loft, the stables' mirror
the kitchen garden is walled and moves under the terrace
the training yard moves to the south-east, the paddock's mirror
the champions: two instead of seven, at the grand stair
go: the west wing (its chapel moves next to the keep, its armory to the barracks)
the inner curtain, its two towers and the two ward gates
the postern and the belvedere (the west moat takes their ground)
new: the terrace and the grand stair
the moat, its springs and the south fall
the bridge, the gate terrace, the ledge walk and the lookout
the privy garden and the muster yard

camera.facts: game.ts updateCamera: 21 up and 14 back from the hero per zoom step (0.65 to 1.35), looking 1 m over the hero, 42 degree field of view: it looks down at 55 degrees and shows about 17 m ahead of the hero and 9 m behind, 33 m across, at zoom 1 (23 m ahead at 1.35)
camera.keep: the keep is never seen whole in play: from the fountain it is beyond the top of the screen even zoomed out; from the grand stair the turrets' feet and the frontispiece fill the top of the screen; at the great door the turrets frame an 8 m door. Its height shows from the approach, the island, the title screen and the overview
camera.moat: from the bridge and the ledge road the moat fills the middle of the screen, two metres down between its coping and the drums
camera.inside_mass: standing at the great hall's dais (x 60..62) or the chapel's west end (x 90..92), the camera lands inside a front turret of the keep: the north range must open as one building (hall, keep and chapel cut away together), as the range and kitchen do today

walking.climb: about 26 m for its 11 m rise, a little steeper than today (one hairpin would restore today's grade)

owner_notes.note: castle more grand and epic, stand out from the other buildings
owner_notes.answer: the great keep: 28 m to its parapet, turrets 34.5, spires 44; everything else 14 m or lower (wings 11.5 and 14, curtain 8.4, towers 13.8 and 21.5 with spires, stables and barracks 6.5)

owner_notes.note: main building: window placement boring, copy-paste
owner_notes.answer: one showpiece window over the great door; sizes fall storey by storey (tall lancets, paired lights, small lights); slit lights stepping up the turrets; every other building its own window type (hall: paired windows between buttresses, chapel: lancets and a rose window, kitchen: small high lights, solar: an oriel, stables: half-doors)

owner_notes.note: donjon repetitive; the cylinder beside the building does not fit
owner_notes.answer: the donjon and the door turret go; the round forms are the keep's own four corner turrets, one composition
the inner curtain and its towers go; twelve towers and the gatehouse, mirrored

owner_notes.note: the other side has almost no towers, unbalanced, not centred
owner_notes.answer: west and east faces mirror each other: three wall towers each at the quarter points, 21.5 m apart; the south face 23 m apart

owner_notes.note: the tower door is crammed in
owner_notes.answer: the stair tower goes; the wall walk is reached through the gatehouse's drums

owner_notes.note: stables: weird spot for the trough and the cones; horses need room
owner_notes.answer: a working stable yard (no ornaments) with the trough against the stable wall; the paddock 20 by 25 behind the stables, three times today's

owner_notes.note: kitchen garden: weird door and pillar; disconnected corner
owner_notes.answer: walled square under the terrace on its own axis: the stair comes down into it, gates on the walk and the stable yard; no tower in it, every bed reached

owner_notes.note: landing: wall on the other side of the path, a moat flowing to the river; needs wall; grass discontinuity
owner_notes.answer: the moat runs between the castle and the road; the road has walls on both sides; the moat falls to the stream under the gate terrace; the landing is walled all round but its two openings; the crown's turf runs unbroken to the moat's coping

owner_notes.note: sunken tree; little trees need variety
owner_notes.answer: for the trees work: trees seated on their ground; in the castle yews, blossom trees, shade trees and fruit trees on the kitchen garden walls

owner_notes.note: helmets, too many gold diamonds, flag short, flag shadow, dragon forelegs
owner_notes.answer: carried into the build: new champion helmets (two champions only), the diamond only on banners and flags, the keep's banners 12 m long, the great flag on the keep (its shadow falls behind the keep), the dragon's forelegs reworked

build_stages.name: ground plan
build_stages.what: the castle's plan moves out of buildKeep into its own module split by area (plan constants, ground and water, approach, bailey dressing, building specs) so later stages edit separate files; the new axis, curtain, towers, gatehouse position, terrace levels with built edges, moat cells, crown and island outline, the approach cells and climb, the farm and stream moves; today's kit placed at the new positions (curtain, drum towers, gatehouse, fountain, parterre), the keep and the wings as plain enterable buildings in today's style; tests (symmetry, connected walks, geometry audit) and the inspect views updated

build_stages.name: the great keep
build_stages.what: its own model: frontispiece, pinnacles, showpiece window, storey-by-storey windows, machicolated parapet, four turrets with stair lights and spires, great door, banners, great flag; interior: throne hall, dais, piers, two stairs, galleries; the north range opens as one round the hero

build_stages.name: moat and water
build_stages.what: moat surface and revetment with its coping, the springs at its heads, the weir, culvert and outlet arch, the south fall and pool, the west overflow fall, the stream's new head

build_stages.name: approach and gate front
build_stages.what: the ledge road's two walls, the gate terrace bastion with lamps and banner poles, the bridge (two arches and a drawbridge span), the landing and the lookout, the ledge walk, the climb's bend
files: the approach part of the castle plan module

build_stages.name: bailey grounds
build_stages.what: the narrower parterre, the walled kitchen and privy gardens (walls, gates, beds, well, basin, arbour), stable and muster yards, paddock and training yard (fences, gates, pells, butts, horses), trees, lamps, kerbs
files: the bailey dressing part of the castle plan module

build_stages.name: the other buildings
build_stages.what: the great hall (today's range turned round), the kitchen moved, the chapel and the solar, the stables and barracks; each its own window scheme

build_stages.name: carried details
build_stages.what: champion helmets, fewer gold diamonds, long banners, the dragon's forelegs, clear tinted glass (with the stone work)

build_stages.name: together
build_stages.what: CASTLE_DESIGN.md, the inspect suite's views, the owner's picture review

painting_departures: flat roofs behind parapets on every castle building (the standing rule) instead of the painting's steep slate roofs
one fall on the axis under the gate terrace instead of two either side of the bridge: the water has one way out to the stream
the approach keeps today's climb and ledge road instead of a straight causeway up the cliff
the keep's back stands on the north brink and the hall and the chapel are mirrored either side of it, where the painting has a hall on one side only
no cottage houses round the forecourt: the service buildings stand along the side walls, so the axis stays open
the gate drums stay flat with flags; only the corner towers and the keep carry spires (the painting gives every tower one)
the moat lies two metres down between built banks rather than brimming at the foot of the walls
